name: Boquete
description: Panama's most famous coffee district on the eastern slopes of Volcán Barú. The unique micro-climate — driven by cool trade winds and the daily 'bajareque' mist — creates ideal conditions for slow cherry development.
climateNotes: Cool trade winds and daily bajareque mist moderate temperature swings and extend cherry maturation on the eastern slopes of Volcán Barú.
terroir: Eastern Barú slopes with afternoon cloud cover

name: Tierras Altas
description: The western slopes of Volcán Barú, encompassing Volcán, Cerro Punta, and Bambito. Drier and windier with some of Panama's highest coffee growing ground above 2,000 MASL.
climateNotes: Exposure to Pacific-seasonality, wind, and high-elevation plateaus produces a drier mountain climate with some of Panama's highest coffee farms.

name: Renacimiento
description: Panama's northwestern-most coffee district bordering Costa Rica. Caribbean moisture influence produces a more humid environment. Home to Finca Hartmann and exceptional biodiversity alongside primary rainforest fragments.
climateNotes: Caribbean moisture and shade-cooled valleys create a more humid mesoclimate with slower drying and abundant biodiversity near forest fragments.
